name: Häselgehr
kurzbeschreibung: Rural community in the Lechtal valley, featuring a Baroque church and historic farmsteads.
beschreibung:
Overview

Häselgehr is situated at 1,006 metres above sea level in the middle Lech Valley in the district of Reutte, Außerfern. The municipal area encompasses approximately 50 square kilometres and is home to around 680 inhabitants. Nestled within the Naturpark Tiroler Lech, one of Central Europe's last pristine wild river landscapes, the village borders wide gravel banks and lush riparian forests along the Lech River. Flanked by the rugged massifs of the Lechtal and Allgäu Alps, Häselgehr offers a quiet, nature-focused haven. The municipality comprises several historic hamlets including Ort, Gutschau, and Ebele, and marks the gateway to the valley leading to Gramais, Austria's smallest independent municipality.

History

The settlement of the upper Lech Valley was established in the High Middle Ages primarily by Alemannic settlers arriving from the Allgäu region. Häselgehr was first documented in 1358 under the name Heselgêr, an etymological combination of hazel bushes and gehr, signifying a wedge-shaped parcel of land. For centuries, rural life was defined by subsistence mountain farming, compelling many locals to seek work abroad as seasonal plasterers, stonemasons, or child labourers. The town's crowning architectural treasure is the Parish Church of St. Martin, celebrated far and wide as the Lechtal Cathedral (Lechtaler Dom) due to its impressive size and rich late-Baroque splendour. Constructed in the late 18th century, it showcases breathtaking ceiling frescoes created by the celebrated master painter Johann Jakob Zeiller.

Getting There

By car, Häselgehr is reached from the north via Reutte along the Lechtal Road B198 heading upvalley. From the Inn Valley in summer, travellers can take the scenic mountain road across the Hahntennjoch pass from Imst to Elmen, continuing onto Häselgehr (closed during winter). From Vorarlberg, access runs via the Arlberg or Flexen Pass through Warth into the Lechtal. By rail, passengers travel to Reutte in Tirol station or Füssen station in Bavaria. From Reutte, VVT regional bus line 110 runs regularly along the valley directly to Häselgehr, stopping in the village centre and adjoining hamlets.

Tips

A mysterious natural spectacle is the Doser Waterfall tucked away in the Tuill gorge: According to local lore and karst hydrology, this underground spring bursts forth reliably around St. George's Day (April 23) and dries up around St. Martin's Day (November 11). Hikers value Häselgehr as an attractive stage along the 125-kilometre Lechweg long-distance trail, following the wild river from its source to the Lech Falls. Art enthusiasts should not miss exploring the interior of the Lechtal Cathedral. In addition, an excursion up the narrow mountain lane to the secluded hamlet of Gramais reveals well-preserved wooden log farmhouses exemplifying authentic Alpine heritage.
